entry.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
entry.summary:
Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #neuroscience #agents

entry.title: Bioprocess Modeling Made Easy With Hybrax
entry.summary:
Hybrid models that embed neural networks in ordinary differential equations are increasingly popular in bioprocess modeling, but they are challenging to set up. Much of the effort goes into the code around the model: wet-lab data must be imported and pre-processed, feeds and sampling must be accounted for in the balance equations, and a training loop with cross-validation must be set up. Researchers usually write this code from scratch for each project.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #neuroscience

entry.title: Generalized Batched Decomposition Key-Switching for CKKS. In lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes, ciphertexts carry an inherent noise that grows as computation advances.
entry.summary:
In lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes, ciphertexts carry an inherent noise that grows as computation advances. The key-switching procedure of these schemes allows the homomorphic re-encryption of a ciphertext under a new secret key, but it incurs substantial noise growth and computational cost. In this work, we generalize the RNS-based decomposition technique of the CKKS scheme to an arbitrary number of input polynomials and secret keys.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #neuroscience

entry.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01075-w This study presents a scalable, efficient framework for unconventional computing with physical neural networks. It replaces dense connections with uncoupled one-dimensional dynamics, simplifies training, improves performance and reduces resource use.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #neuroscience
